mainTopic: The end of the discussion on when a thief stops paying ארבעה וחמשה after a court ruling, and the start of a new discussion of רבי יוחנן's rule that stolen property that the owner has not given up on (no יאוש) cannot be made הקדש by either the thief or the owner.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבא's point. If the court only told the thief 'you are obligated to give it back' and he then slaughtered or sold the animal, he still pays ארבעה וחמשה, because the case was not final and he is still a גנב. The גמרא uses this to answer the challenge against ריש לקיש. Next it returns to רבי יוחנן's rule: before יאוש, neither the thief nor the owner can make a stolen item הקדש. This is challenged from רבי יוחנן's own rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. The משנה in question explains how vineyards and graves are marked and says that the צנועין redeem fruit that passersby 'have picked,' which seems to show an owner acting on something no longer in his hands. The גמרא considers attributing this line to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל alone, but rejects that defense because רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in our משנה. It answers instead by reading it as 'will be picked.' That answer is challenged from רבי יוחנן's statement linking the צנועין to רבי דוסא, so the גמרא reverses the ברייתא of רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא. It explains that the ברייתא must be reversed because רבי יהודה rejects ברירה, and the proof from a משנה comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A thief told only 'you are obligated to give' still pays four or five times
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his distinction. If the court only said 'you are obligated to give it to him' and the thief then slaughtered or sold the animal, he still pays ארבעה וחמשה, because the case was not finalized and he is still a גנב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the court only told him 'You are obligated to give it to him,' and then he slaughtered or sold the animal, he pays four or five times. Why? Since the matter was not settled, he is still a thief!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is finishing his rule about how strong a court statement must be before a גנב stops paying ארבעה וחמשה. A weak statement ('you are obligated') does not change his status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a final court order turns the stolen animal into something the thief simply owes, like a גזלן's debt. The words 'you are obligated to give' declare who is right but do not close the case. So the thief is still a regular גנב and owes the full four or five times.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtered or sold the stolen animal, which is what triggers the extra payment.
The four-times or five-times penalty payment for a stolen sheep or ox that was slaughtered or sold.
The matter was finalized or decided.
A thief who steals secretly, as opposed to a robber (גַּזְלָן) who takes openly.

phrases.english: If the court said 'You are obligated to give it to him,' and he slaughtered or sold it
he pays the fourfold or fivefold payment.
What is the reason?
Since the matter was not finalized,
he is still a thief!

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיב אַתָּה לִיתֵּן לוֹ טָבַח וּמָכַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's statement, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After only 'you are obligated to give,' the thief remains a גנב and pays ארבעה וחמשה if he slaughters or sells.

steps.title: The ברייתא speaks of a court that only said 'you are obligated'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the earlier challenge to ריש לקיש. The ברייתא that has the thief paying ארבעה וחמשה after going to court is talking about a case where the court only said 'you are obligated to give it to him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the case where they said to him only: 'You are obligated to give it to him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבא's distinction to solve the earlier challenge. The ברייתא is read as speaking about the weaker court statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the ברייתא meant a final court order, which would contradict ריש לקיש. By limiting the ברייתא to 'you are obligated,' it no longer clashes with him: in that case the thief is still a גנב and naturally pays four or five times.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is only needed for...', which narrows a source to one specific case.
That they (the court) said to him.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think 'you are obligated to give' and 'go, give it to him' are the same thing. Only the firm order 'go, give' takes him out of the status of a גנב.
steps.whatToRemember: A court statement changes the thief's status only if it is a final order ('go, give'). A declaration of obligation alone leaves him a גנב who pays ארבעה וחמשה.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary
where they say to him: 'You are obligated to give it to him.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבא's distinction from step 1 to answer the challenge against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that even after a final court order the thief pays ארבעה וחמשה, against ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a court that only said 'you are obligated,' so the thief is still a גנב and there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Stolen item before the owner gives up: no one can consecrate it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי יוחנן's statement. If something was stolen and the owner has not despaired, neither the thief nor the owner can make it הקדש. The thief cannot because it is not his, and the owner cannot because it is not in his possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: Getting back to the main point, רבי יוחנן said: If someone stole and the owner has not despaired, neither of them can consecrate it. This one (the thief), because it isn't his; and that one (the owner), because it isn't in his possession.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a statement of רבי יוחנן quoted earlier in passing, in order to examine it on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To make something הקדש you need two things: it must be yours, and it must be in your possession. Before יאוש, the thief has possession but not ownership. The owner has ownership but not possession. Since each is missing one piece, neither can consecrate it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Returning to the matter itself.' The גמרא goes back to examine a statement it mentioned earlier.
The owner's giving up hope of getting the item back.
To consecrate something to the בית המקדש.
In his possession or control.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that הקדש needs both ownership and possession. That idea is what the following challenge puts to the test.

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If one stole and the owner has not despaired,
neither of them is able to consecrate it.
This one, because it is not his,
and that one, because it is not in his possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to a statement of רבי יוחנן cited earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before יאוש, neither the thief nor the owner can consecrate the stolen item.

steps.title: Did רבי יוחנן really say this, given his rule about a סתם משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוחנן really said this. He himself holds that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and it is about to bring a סתם משנה that seems to disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did רבי יוחנן really say that? Didn't רבי יוחנן say: the הלכה follows an unattributed משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against רבי יוחנן from his own rule. This line sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן always follows a סתם משנה, then a סתם משנה that goes against his statement creates a contradiction inside his own views. The specific משנה is quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And did he really say so?' This opens a challenge from the same Sage's other views.
The הלכה follows a משנה stated without any Sage's name attached.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yoḥanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say:
the halakha follows an unattributed mishna;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the owner cannot consecrate a stolen item before יאוש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן follows a סתם משנה, and a סתם משנה (quoted next) seems to rule differently, so his views appear to contradict each other.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about marking a fourth-year vineyard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the סתם משנה from מסכת מעשר שני. People used to mark a vineyard in its fourth year with clods of earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: A vineyard in its fourth year, they would mark it with clods of earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the משנה that will be used against רבי יוחנן. The part that causes the difficulty comes later in this משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fruit of a כרם רבעי may not be eaten until it is redeemed, so people marked the vineyard to warn passersby. This opening line only sets the scene. The challenge itself comes from what the משנה says next.

keyTerms.meaning: A vineyard in its fourth year. Its fruit must be eaten in ירושלים or redeemed.
They would mark it.
Clods of earth.

phrases.english: And we learned: A vineyard in its fourth year,
they would mark it
with clods of earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן כֶּרֶם רְבָעִי הָיוּ מְצַיְּינִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the סתם משנה promised in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That a סתם משנה seems to contradict רבי יוחנן's ruling.

steps.title: Why the mark is made of earth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses its quote to explain the sign. A כרם רבעי is like earth: just as one may benefit from earth, so too this fruit may be used once it is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sign is like earth: just as earth can be benefited from, so too this fruit, once it is redeemed, may be benefited from.
steps.whatsHappening: In the middle of quoting the משנה, the גמרא adds a short explanation of why clods of earth were chosen as the sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sign hints at the law of what it marks. Earth is something people use and benefit from, which hints that this fruit is not forbidden forever. It only needs פדיון, and after that it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: A sign or marker.
When it is redeemed (פִּדְיוֹן).
It is permitted to benefit from it.

steps.confusionAlert: This explanation is the גמרא's own aside. It is not part of the משנה's words, and the quote of the משנה continues afterward.

phrases.english: The sign is like earth:
just as earth
there is benefit from it,
phrases.notes: He means you can grow things in earth and get use from it.

phrases.english: so too this, when it is redeemed,
it is permitted to benefit from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An explanation inserted into the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The earth marker hints that כרם רבעי fruit becomes permitted for benefit once it is redeemed.

steps.title: The sign for ערלה is broken pottery
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: an ערלה vineyard is marked with broken pottery. It explains that just as no benefit comes from broken pottery, no benefit is allowed from ערלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And an ערלה vineyard is marked with broken pottery. That is the sign because ערלה is like broken pottery: just as you get no benefit from broken pottery, so too you may get no benefit from this fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה and stops again to explain why this sign was chosen. It does the same thing it did for כרם רבעי in step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sign fits the law of the fruit it marks. Earth (step 6) is something you can use, which matches כרם רבעי, since its fruit may be used once redeemed. Broken pottery is useless, which matches ערלה, since no benefit at all is allowed from it.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years. It is completely forbidden, even for benefit.
Broken pieces of pottery.
Benefit or use.
A sign or marker.

phrases.english: And a vineyard of ערלה is marked with broken pottery.
The sign is like broken pottery,
just as broken pottery gives no benefit,
so too this fruit may give no benefit.
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, but some versions leave it out. The meaning is the same either way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This follows the pattern of step 6. The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and explains the sign it mentions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ערלה vineyard is marked with broken pottery, which shows that no benefit is allowed from it.

steps.title: The sign for graves is lime, mixed with water
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says graves are marked with lime. The גמרא explains that lime is white like bones, and that it is mixed with water and poured out so it looks even whiter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a grave area is marked with lime. That is the sign because lime is white like bones. And you dissolve the lime in water and pour it out, so that it will be even whiter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the משנה with the sign used for graves. It explains both why lime is used and why it is mixed with water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White lime makes people think of bones, so they know a grave is there and can avoid becoming טמא. Dissolving the lime and pouring it makes the mark stand out even more.

keyTerms.meaning: Graves.
Lime, a white powder.
Bones.
Dissolves or mixes into water.

phrases.english: And an area of graves is marked with lime.
The sign is that it is white, like bones.
And one dissolves it and pours it out
so that it will be whiter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This keeps going through the משנה's list of signs. The next item is graves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Graves are marked with white lime, dissolved in water so it is whiter, because it looks like bones.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: marking is only needed in שביעית
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the משנה: the vineyards only need to be marked in שביעית. The גמרא adds the reason: in that year the fruit is הפקר, so anyone may take it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When does this rule apply? In שביעית, because then the fruit is ownerless.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now adds a limit to the marking rule. This is still background: the line that actually challenges רבי יוחנן, about the צנועין, comes in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית everyone is allowed to pick the fruit. Honest people may come and eat it, so they need to be warned that it is כרם רבעי or ערלה. The words 'because it is ownerless' are the גמרא's short explanation added inside the quote.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When does this apply?' A phrase used to narrow a rule.
The seventh year of the farming cycle, when fields are left open to everyone.
Ownerless. Anyone may take it.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in ordinary years, anyone who takes the fruit is stealing it. That sets up the צנועין line in step 11, where the owner redeems fruit that passersby have taken.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: 'These words' means the rule about marking כרם רבעי and ערלה vineyards.

phrases.english: In the Sabbatical Year, because the fruits are ownerless;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After listing the signs, the משנה now limits when they are required.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יוחנן's rule (step 3) fits with the סתם משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סתם משנה in מסכת מעשר שני, with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's limit.

steps.title: In other years, there is no need to warn the thief
steps.stepSummary: In the other years of the seven-year cycle, anyone taking the fruit is stealing. So there is no need to mark the vineyard, as the saying goes: 'Feed it to the wicked man and let him die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But in the other years of the seven-year cycle: feed it to the wicked man, and let him die.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its point. In normal years we do not bother warning a thief that the fruit he is stealing is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In normal years only a thief would take the fruit, since it belongs to the owner. We do not need to protect a thief from an extra sin, so no sign is needed. The משנה continues in the next step with the צנועין, and that is the line that challenges רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The years of the seven-year farming cycle.
'Feed it to the wicked man and let him die.' We do not need to protect a sinner from his own wrongdoing.

steps.whatToRemember: The signs: earth for כרם רבעי (it can be used once redeemed), broken pottery for ערלה (no benefit allowed), and lime for graves (white like bones). According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, marking is only needed in שביעית, when the fruit is הפקר. In other years, only thieves take the fruit, and we do not need to warn them.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Let him die' is a saying, not a death penalty. It just means we do not have to protect a thief from the extra sin of eating forbidden fruit.

phrases.english: But in the other years of the seven-year cycle,
feed it to the wicked man and let him die.
phrases.notes: The 'wicked man' is the thief. Only a thief would take the fruit in a normal year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement by describing the other years.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יוחנן's rule (step 3) fits with the סתם משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The end of the סתם משנה: in non-שביעית years, fruit is not marked to warn thieves.

steps.title: The pious ones redeem fruit already taken by passersby
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: the צנועין set aside coins and declare that whatever was picked from their vineyard is redeemed onto those coins. This sounds like an owner can act on fruit that has left his possession, which challenges רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the pious ones set aside coins and say: 'Whatever was picked from this vineyard is redeemed onto these coins.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and uses it as a challenge against רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Passersby already took the fruit, so it is no longer in the owner's hands. Even so, the צנועין redeem it, and the redemption works. That goes against רבי יוחנן's view that an owner cannot act on something that has left his possession, such as a stolen item.

keyTerms.meaning: Pious, extra-careful people
Coins
Was picked (past tense)
Redeemed; its holiness moves onto something else

phrases.english: And the pious ones would set aside coins,
and say: "Anything that was picked from this [vineyard]
is redeemed onto these coins"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same משנה, and this line becomes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that an owner cannot act on an item no longer in his possession
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The צנועין redeem fruit that passersby already took, and the משנה treats this as effective.

steps.title: Maybe this is only the opinion of a single sage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a defense. The צנועין line belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and רבי יוחנן only follows an unnamed משנה when it is not one sage's personal view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: Who taught the line about the pious ones? It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. And רבי יוחנן did not rule like an unnamed משנה that reflects only one sage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out for רבי יוחנן. The next step will knock it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's rule is that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. But this line comes right after רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement, so it may be his own individual view. If so, רבי יוחנן's rule does not force him to accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a suggested answer)
Who taught this?
An unnamed משנה, given with no sage's name
A single, individual sage

phrases.english: And if you would say: Who taught [the line about] the pious ones?
It is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל,
phrases.notes: His statement in Steps 9–10 comes right before this line in the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כִּסְתָם יְחִידָאָה לָא אָמַר;
phrases.english: and רבי יוחנן did not say [the הלכה follows] an unnamed משנה that is an individual's view;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A suggested defense against the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the source to an individual sage, so רבי יוחנן's rule does not cover it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The צנועין line looks like a סתם משנה that רבי יוחנן must follow
steps.terutzMaskana: It may be רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's individual view, which רבי יוחנן need not accept

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in our משנה
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion fails. רבי יוחנן himself said that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wherever he appears in our משנה, except in three cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן: Wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught in our משנה, the הלכה follows him, except for the case of the guarantor, the case of צידן, and the last proof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense from Step 12 by quoting another ruling of רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if this line belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, רבי יוחנן holds that the הלכה follows him in our משנה. This case is not one of the three exceptions. So the challenge from the צנועין comes back at full strength.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (introduces a counter-source)
The הלכה follows him
A guarantor on a loan
The last proof (a case about bringing evidence later)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two rules of רבי יוחנן. One is that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה. The other is that the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in our משנה. Step 12 dodged the first rule, but this step uses the second rule to close the gap.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say that רבי יוחנן said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁשָּׁנָה רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בְּמִשְׁנָתֵנוּ
phrases.english: Wherever רבן שמעון בן גמליאל taught in our משנה,
the הלכה is like him,
except for the guarantor, צידן, and the last proof!
phrases.notes: These are three known cases: בבא בתרא 173b, גיטין 74a, and סנהדרין 31a.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense offered in Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that calling it רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view frees רבי יוחנן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוחנן rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in our משנה, and this case is not one of the exceptions

steps.title: Read it as fruit that will be picked
steps.stepSummary: The answer is to change the wording. The צנועין say 'whatever will be picked', so the redemption takes effect while the fruit is still on the vine and in the owner's possession.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Don't say 'whatever was picked from this'. Rather, say 'whatever will be picked from this'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by fixing the wording of the צנועין's declaration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the redemption works on fruit that will be picked, the owner acts while the fruit still belongs to him. That fits perfectly with רבי יוחנן. The משנה no longer shows an owner acting on something that left his hands.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say this, rather say that (a wording fix)
Will be picked (future)

steps.whatToRemember: The צנועין redeem the fruit in advance, before it is picked. So the redemption happens while the owner still has it, and רבי יוחנן's view stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a small change in tense can decide whether a source supports a view or contradicts it.

phrases.english: They say: Do not say "anything that was picked from this,"
rather say "anything that will be picked from this."
phrases.notes: So the coins take on the holiness ahead of time, while the grapes are still on the owner's vine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא תֵּימָא ״כׇּל הַנִּלְקָט מִזֶּה״, אֶלָּא אֵימָא ״כָּל הַמִּתְלַקֵּט מִזֶּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first defense failed in Step 13, this gives the real answer to Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording from past tense to future tense
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The צנועין redeem fruit already taken, which is out of the owner's possession
steps.terutzMaskana: They redeem fruit before it is picked, while it is still in the owner's possession

steps.title: רבי יוחנן Linked the צנועין to רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the future-tense reading of step 14. רבי יוחנן said the צנועין and רבי דוסא hold the same view, and רבי דוסא uses the past tense, "was picked."
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But he said that the צנועין and רבי דוסא said the same thing, and רבי דוסא speaks about what "was picked"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It brings another statement of רבי יוחנן that seems to force the צנועין's words into the past tense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the צנועין's words were read as future tense, so they act on fruit still in the owner's possession. But רבי יוחנן said the צנועין match רבי דוסא, who speaks in the past tense. If so, the צנועין would also be acting on fruit already taken, and the original problem for רבי יוחנן comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really say this? A way of doubting that a sage would hold this view.
But didn't he say...? Brings a contradicting statement.
The same thing; the two opinions match.
Was picked (past tense)

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan really say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:

phrases.aramaic: צְנוּעִין וְרַבִּי דּוֹסָא אָמְרוּ דָּבָר אֶחָד;
phrases.english: The pious ones and Rabbi Dosa said the same thing;
and Rabbi Dosa says "was picked"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the future-tense rewording given in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the צנועין said "whatever will be picked" (future tense).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן equates the צנועין with רבי דוסא. רבי דוסא uses the past tense, so the צנועין must also be past tense, and that conflicts with רבי יוחנן's own rule.

steps.title: The ברייתא: Morning Declaration vs. Evening Declaration
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי דוסא's declaration is made in the evening and uses the past tense. רבי יהודה's declaration is made in the morning and uses the future tense.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says that in the morning the owner of the field declares, "Whatever the poor will pick today shall be הפקר." רבי דוסא says that toward evening he declares, "Whatever the poor picked shall be הפקר."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי דוסא speaks in the past tense. This gives the challenge from step 15 its force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Poor people may take some produce from a field, and some may take more than they are allowed. The owner declares that produce הפקר so they are not stealing. רבי יהודה has him do it in advance ("will pick"), while רבי דוסא has him do it afterward ("picked"). That past-tense wording is what creates the problem.

keyTerms.meaning: In the morning
The owner (here, the owner of the field)
Ownerless; anyone may take it
Toward evening

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
In the morning, the owner stands and says:
"Whatever the poor will pick today
phrases.notes: He means produce the poor take beyond what they're really entitled to.

phrases.english: shall be ownerless."

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי דּוֹסָא אוֹמֵר, לְעִיתּוֹתֵי עֶרֶב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Dosa says: toward evening he says:
"Whatever the poor picked shall be ownerless"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא source behind the claim in step 15 that רבי דוסא says "was picked."
steps.raayaObject: That רבי דוסא's declaration is in the past tense.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי דוסא about when and how the owner declares הפקר.

steps.title: Swap the Opinions in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by reversing the ברייתא. רבי דוסא gets the morning, future-tense declaration, and רבי יהודה gets the evening, past-tense one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse the opinion of רבי יהודה to רבי דוסא, and the opinion of רבי דוסא to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by switching which sage said what in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the swap, רבי דוסא says "whatever the poor will pick." Since the צנועין match רבי דוסא, they also speak in the future tense. This fits step 14 and keeps רבי יוחנן consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse; switch the opinions between the two sages

phrases.english: Reverse Rabbi Yehuda's view to Rabbi Dosa,
and Rabbi Dosa's view to Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversing the names attached to the opinions in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי דוסא says the past-tense "whatever the poor picked," so the צנועין are past tense too.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי דוסא actually says the future-tense "whatever the poor will pick," so the צנועין are future tense, as step 14 said.

steps.title: Why Not Switch רבי יוחנן's Statement Instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we change the ברייתא. It would be simpler to change רבי יוחנן's statement to say that the צנועין match רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do you reverse the ברייתא? Reverse רבי יוחנן's statement instead, and say: "The צנועין and רבי יהודה said the same thing"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the method of the answer it just gave. It offers what looks like an easier fix and sets up a reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both fixes reach the same result: the צנועין are linked to the future-tense declaration. The question is which text should be changed. Changing one line of רבי יוחנן seems simpler than reversing a whole ברייתא, so the גמרא needs a reason for its choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
A teaching of the תנאים; here, the ברייתא
And say instead...

steps.confusionAlert: This question does not deny that the צנועין speak in the future tense. It agrees with that. It only asks which text should be changed to get there.

phrases.english: Why do you reverse the baraita?
phrases.notes: מַתְנִיתָא here means the ברייתא we just quoted, not our משנה.

phrases.english: Reverse Rabbi Yochanan's statement instead,
and say:
"The pious ones and Rabbi Yehuda said the same thing"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי אָפְכַתְּ מַתְנִיתָא? אִפְכַהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the method used in step 17's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to reverse the ברייתא rather than רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Changing רבי יוחנן's statement to link the צנועין with רבי יהודה, who already uses the future tense, gives the same result with less disruption to the ברייתא.

steps.title: The ברייתא must be reversed because רבי יהודה rejects ברירה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that reversing the ברייתא is unavoidable. The original wording would have רבי יהודה accept ברירה, but elsewhere he rejects it. A משנה is about to be quoted as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: We have no choice but to reverse the ברייתא. As written, this ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה holds of ברירה. But we have heard from elsewhere that רבי יהודה generally does not hold of ברירה, as we learned in a משנה:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 18: we cannot just change רבי יוחנן's words, because the ברייתא itself must be reversed. It ends by setting up a משנה that will prove the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the original ברייתא, רבי יהודה uses the future tense, "whatever the poor will pick." That only works with ברירה, since which produce the poor end up picking later decides what became הפקר in the morning. Since רבי יהודה elsewhere rejects ברירה, that version cannot be right, so the ברייתא must be flipped.

keyTerms.meaning: Retroactive clarification: a later event reveals what was chosen or designated earlier
There is no way around it; it cannot be otherwise
Is reversed or flipped
In general; elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word מַתְנִיתָא and the word מַתְנִיתִין both refer to the ברייתא from step 16, not to our משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step shows that the גמרא keeps each תנא consistent with his known positions. A text is reversed only when leaving it alone would make a תנא contradict himself.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: לָא סַגִּיא דְּלָא מִתְהַפְכָא מַתְנִיתָא;
phrases.english: They say: There is no choice but that the ברייתא must be reversed;
phrases.notes: This answers step 18's question: why not change רבי יוחנן's words instead?

phrases.english: for in this ברייתא it teaches
that רבי יהודה holds of ברירה,
phrases.notes: In the original version, רבי יהודה says "what the poor will pick." What they end up picking later decides what became הפקר in the morning, and that is ברירה.

phrases.english: and we have heard regarding רבי יהודה elsewhere
that he does not hold of ברירה, as we learned in a משנה:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא סַגִּיא דְּלָא מִתְהַפְכָא מַתְנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers step 18's question about why the ברייתא was reversed rather than רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.terutzResolutionType: It defends the earlier change to the text by showing that the original version would make רבי יהודה contradict himself.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It would be simpler to change רבי יוחנן's statement so that the צנועין match רבי יהודה, and leave the ברייתא alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא must be reversed anyway, because as written it has רבי יהודה accepting ברירה, which he rejects elsewhere.
